arxiv-2101-07679.title: The Six Hug Commandments: Design and Evaluation of a Human-Sized Hugging Robot with Visual and Haptic Perception DOI: 10.1145/3434073.3444656 Conference: Proceedings of the 2021 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction; March 8–11, 2021; Boulder, CO, USA Proceedings of the 2021 A
arxiv-2101-07679.creator: Alexis E. Block, Sammy Christen, Roger Gassert, Otmar Hilliges, Katherine J. Kuchenbecker
arxiv-2101-07679.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexis E. Block, Sammy Christen, Roger Gassert, Otmar Hilliges, Katherine J. Kuchenbecker. Receiving a hug is one of the best ways to feel socially supported, and the lack of social touch can have severe negative effects on an individual’s well-being.

arxiv-2103-12288.title: On a generalized Brauer group in mixed characteristic cases, II
arxiv-2103-12288.creator: Makoto Sakagaito
arxiv-2103-12288.description: Abstract As an extension of an author’s previous paper ( [ 20 , Theorem 1.1] ), we prove the Gersten-type conjecture for the mod p p étale motivic cohomology over a local ring of a smooth scheme over the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic ( 0 , p ) (0,p) .

arxiv-2105-04649.title: Symmetry Protected Quantum Computation
arxiv-2105-04649.creator: M. H. Freedman, M. B. Hastings, M. Shokrian Zini
arxiv-2105-04649.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. H. Freedman, M. B. Hastings, M. Shokrian Zini. We consider a model of quantum computation using qubits where it is possible to measure whether a given pair are in a singlet (total spin 0 0 ) or triplet (total spin 1 1 ) state. The physical motivation is that we can do these measurements in a way that is protected against revealing other information so long as all terms in the Hamiltonian are S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) -invariant.

arxiv-2109-13696.title: Improving Time Series Classification Algorithms Using Octave-Convolutional Layers
arxiv-2109-13696.creator: Samuel Harford, Fazle Karim, Houshang Darabi
arxiv-2109-13696.description: Abstract Deep learning models utilizing convolution layers have achieved state-of-the-art performance on univariate time series classification tasks. In this work, we propose improving CNN based time series classifiers by utilizing Octave Convolutions (OctConv) to outperform themselves. These network architectures include Fully Convolutional Networks (FCN), Residual Neural Networks (ResNets), LSTM-Fully Convolutional Networks (LSTM-FCN), and Attention LSTM-Fully Convolutional Networks (ALSTM-FCN).

arxiv-2111-02190.title: Thermo-magneto-electric transport through a torsion dislocation in a type I Weyl Semimetal
arxiv-2111-02190.creator: Daniel Bonilla, Enrique Muñoz, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido
arxiv-2111-02190.description: Abstract We study electronic and thermoelectric transport in a type I Weyl semimetal nanojunction, with a torsional dislocation defect, in the presence of an external magnetic field parallel to the dislocation axis. The defect is modeled in a cylindrical geometry, as a combination of a gauge field accounting for torsional strain, and a delta-potential barrier for the lattice mismatch effect.

arxiv-2206-14226.title: Thermal properties of structurally balanced systems on classical random graphs
arxiv-2206-14226.creator: Krzysztof Malarz, Maciej Wołoszyn
arxiv-2206-14226.description: Abstract The dynamics of social relations and the possibility of reaching the state of structural balance (Heider balance) under the influence of the temperature modeling the social noise level are discussed for interacting actors occupying nodes of classical random graphs.

arxiv-2307-00340.title: On relation between renormalized frequency and heat capacity for particles in an anharmonic potential
arxiv-2307-00340.creator: Y. T. Liu, Y. H. Zhao, Y. Zhong, J. M. Shen, J. H. Zhang, Q. H. Liu
arxiv-2307-00340.description: Abstract For free particles in a simple harmonic potential plus a weak anharmonicity, characterized by a set of anharmonic parameters, Newtonian mechanics asserts that there is a renormalization of the natural frequency of the periodic motion; and statistical mechanics claims that the anharmonicity causes a correction to the heat capacity of an ideal gas in the anharmonic potential.

arxiv-2402-05305.title: Knowledge Distillation for Road Detection based on cross-model Semi-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2402-05305.description: Abstract The advancement of knowledge distillation has played a crucial role in enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller and more efficient student models, and is particularly beneficial for online and resource-constrained applications. The effectiveness of the student model heavily relies on the quality of the distilled knowledge received from the teacher.

arxiv-2404-14954.title: Multi-Objective Deep Reinforcement Learning for 5G Base Station Placement to Support Localisation for Future Sustainable Traffic
arxiv-2404-14954.creator: Ahmed Al-Tahmeesschi, Jukka Talvitie, Miguel López-Benítez, Hamed Ahmadi, Laura Ruotsalainen
arxiv-2404-14954.description: Abstract Millimeter-wave (mmWave) is a key enabler for next-generation transportation systems. However, in an urban city scenario, mmWave is highly susceptible to blockages and shadowing. Therefore, base station (BS) placement is a crucial task in the infrastructure design where coverage requirements need to be met while simultaneously supporting localisation.

arxiv-2405-18609.title: Actuators À La Mode: Modal Actuations for Soft Body Locomotion Journal: TOG
arxiv-2405-18609.creator: Otman Benchekroun, Kaixiang Xie, Hsueh-Ti Derek Liu, Eitan Grinspun, Sheldon Andrews, Victor Zordan
arxiv-2405-18609.description: Abstract . Traditional character animation specializes in characters with a rigidly articulated skeleton and a bipedal/quadripedal morphology. This assumption simplifies many aspects for designing physically based animations, like locomotion, but comes with the price of excluding characters of arbitrary deformable geometries.

arxiv-2410-08901.title: SegGrasp: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Grasping via Semantic and Geometric Guided Segmentation
arxiv-2410-08901.creator: Haosheng Li Weixin Mao Weipeng Deng Chenyu Meng Rui Zhang, Fan Jia Tiancai Wang Haoqiang Fan Hongan Wang Xiaoming Deng
arxiv-2410-08901.description: Abstract Task-oriented grasping, which involves grasping specific parts of objects based on their functions, is crucial for developing advanced robotic systems capable of performing complex tasks in dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose a training-free framework that incorporates both semantic and geometric priors for zero-shot task-oriented grasp generation.

arxiv-2411-16529.title: Quantum droplets and Schrödinger’s cat states in atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensates
arxiv-2411-16529.creator: Leena Barshilia 1,2, Rajiuddin Sk 2, Prasanta K. Panigrahi 2, Avinash Khare 3
arxiv-2411-16529.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Leena Barshilia 1,2, Rajiuddin Sk 2, Prasanta K. Panigrahi 2, Avinash Khare 3. Explicit realization of quantum droplets, even and odd Schrödinger cat states is demonstrated in an atom-molecular Bose-Einstein condensate in the presence of interconversion and Kerr non-linear interactions. The crucial roles of both the χ 2 \chi^{2} -type nonlinearity and chemical potential in the formation of these macroscopic quantum states are shown, where the atomic condensate is in the cat state, with the corresponding molecular wave packet being a quantum droplet.

arxiv-2412-19268.title: Jet formation studies in AGN: a search for new targets
arxiv-2412-19268.creator: B. Boccardi, L. Ricci, E. Madika, V. Bartolini, U. Bach, P. Grandi, E. Torresi, T.P. Krichbaum, J. A. Zensus
arxiv-2412-19268.description: Abstract Context. In recent years, the jet formation region in active galaxies has been imaged through mm-VLBI in few ideal targets, first and foremost M 87. An important leap forward for understanding jet launching could be made by identifying a larger number of suitable objects, characterized by different accretion modes and jet powers.

arxiv-2503-20146.title: Speckle-based X-ray microtomography via preconditioned Wirtinger flow
arxiv-2503-20146.creator: KyeoReh Lee, Herve Hugonnet, Jae‑Hong Lim, YongKeun Park
arxiv-2503-20146.description: Abstract Three-dimensional quantitative phase imaging has been extensively studied in X-ray microtomography to improve the sensitivity and specificity of measurements, especially for low atomic number materials. However, obtaining quantitative phase images typically requires additional measurements or assumptions, which significantly limits the practical applicability. Here, we present preconditioned Wirtinger flow (PWF) to realize an assumption-free, single-shot, quantitative X-ray microtomography.

arxiv-2506-04729.title: Galactic Science
arxiv-2506-04729.creator: Sandro Mereghetti
arxiv-2506-04729.description: Abstract The most recent observational and theoretical results in the rapidly expanding field of high-energy gamma-ray astrophysics were discussed at the international conference “Gamma-2024” that took place in Milano in September 2024. This contribution summarises the ’rapporteur talk’ relative to the Galactic science given at the end of the conference.

arxiv-2506-19464.title: Assessing Risk of Stealing Proprietary Models for Medical Imaging Tasks
arxiv-2506-19464.creator: Ankita Raj, Harsh Swaika, Deepankar Varma, Chetan Arora
arxiv-2506-19464.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ankita Raj, Harsh Swaika, Deepankar Varma, Chetan Arora. The success of deep learning in medical imaging applications has led several companies to deploy proprietary models in diagnostic workflows, offering monetized services. Even though model weights are hidden to protect the intellectual property of the service provider, these models are exposed to model stealing (MS) attacks, where adversaries can clone the model’s functionality by querying it with a proxy dataset and training a thief model on the acquired predictions.

arxiv-2509-11492.title: Notebook for the CheckThat! Lab at CLEF 2025
arxiv-2509-11492.creator: Anirban Saha Anik, Md Fahimul Kabir Chowdhury, Andrew Wyckoff, Sagnik Ray Choudhury
arxiv-2509-11492.description: Abstract This paper presents our system for Task 3 of the CLEF 2025 CheckThat! Lab, which focuses on verifying numerical and temporal claims using retrieved evidence. We explore two complementary approaches: zero-shot prompting with instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) and supervised fine-tuning using parameter-efficient LoRA.

arxiv-2509-25868.title: ReFACT: A Benchmark for Scientific Confabulation Detection with Positional Error Annotations
arxiv-2509-25868.creator: Yindong Wang, Martin Preiß, Margarita Bugueño, Jan Vincent Hoffbauer, Abdullatif Ghajar, Tolga Buz, Gerard de Melo
arxiv-2509-25868.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently confabulate scientific facts,severely undermining their trustworthiness. Addressing this challenge requires benchmarks that go beyond binary factuality and enable fine-grained evaluation. We introduce ReFACT ( Reddit False And Correct Texts ), a benchmark of 1,001 expert-annotated question–answer pairs spanning diverse scientific domains for the detection of scientific confabulation.

pmc-10532027.title: The Challenging Differentiation of Psoriatic Arthritis from Other Arthropathies and Nonspecific Arthralgias in Patients with Psoriasis: Results of a Cross-Sectional Rheumatologic Assessment of a Large Dermatologic Cohort
pmc-10532027.creator: Alberto Floris, Cristina Mugheddu, Leonardo Sichi, Martina Dessì, Jasmine Anedda, Alessia Frau, Andrea Pau, Simone Aldo Lari, Jessica Sorgia, Laura Li Volsi, Maria Teresa Paladino, Mattia Congia, Elisabetta Chessa, Maria Maddalena Angioni, Caterina Ferreli, Matteo Piga, Laura Atzori, Alberto Cauli,
pmc-10532027.description: Aiming to identify the potential challenges in the classification of musculoskeletal manifestations in patients with psoriasis (PsO), this study analyzed the outcomes of a cross-sectional rheumatologic assessment of 1057 PsO patients. In total, 209 had a previous diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis (PsA).

pmc-11452096.title: Gene editing in livestock: innovations and applications
pmc-11452096.creator: Paula Rodriguez-Villamil, Benjamin Paul Beaton, Rebecca Lynn Krisher
pmc-11452096.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Gene editing technologies have revolutionized the field of livestock breeding, offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance animal welfare, productivity, and sustainability. This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent innovations and applications of gene editing in livestock, exploring the diverse applications of gene editing in livestock breeding, as well as the regulatory and ethical considerations, and the current challenges and prospects of the technology in the industry.

pmc-11510808.title: Ponte: Represent Totally Binary Neural Network Toward Efficiency
pmc-11510808.creator: Jia Xu, Han Pu, Dong Wang
pmc-11510808.description: In the quest for computational efficiency, binary neural networks (BNNs) have emerged as a promising paradigm, offering significant reductions in memory footprint and computational latency. In traditional BNN implementation, the first and last layers are typically full-precision, which causes higher logic usage in field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation.

pmc-11643957.title: The Biochar Derived from Pecan Shells for the Removal of Congo Red: The Effects of Temperature and Heating Rate
pmc-11643957.creator: Wanqiang Xu, Bo Cai, Xujie Zhang, Yating Zhang, Yongjian Zhang, Hehuan Peng, Antonio Zuorro, Eun Duck Park
pmc-11643957.description: Organic pollutants, especially dyes, are seriously hazardous to the aquatic system and humans due to their toxicity, and carcinogenic or mutagenic properties. In this study, a biochar prepared from agricultural waste (pecan shells) via pyrolysis was applied to remove the dye pollutant Congo Red from wastewater to avoid a negative effect to the ecosystem.

pmc-12659827.title: A novel angulated cannula technique for Laser assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) flap repositioning in left eyes by right-handed surgeons
pmc-12659827.creator: Sudarshan K Khokhar, Amar Pujari, Nisha Yadav, Shivayan Srivastava
pmc-12659827.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is one of the most commonly performed kerato-refractive surgery globally. Over the years we have observed that there has been difficulty in flap reposition using the conventional obtuse blunt cannulas, especially in left eyes of patients by right handed surgeons due to obscuration by the nasal bridge and hence difficult manipulation of the flap often leading to jerky and premature entry beneath the flap. This further leads to flap misalignment or incomplete repositioning.

pmc-13051819.title: Autologous minced cartilage implantation for unstable osteochondritis dissecans of the elbow demonstrates favourable clinical and imaging outcomes at a mean 2‐year follow‐up
pmc-13051819.creator: Tim Leschinger, Tamara Babasiz, Sebastian Wegmann, Felix Krane, Lars P. Müller, Nadine Ott
pmc-13051819.description: PurposeThe minced cartilage technique is a single‐stage cartilage repair option established for focal cartilage defects in larger joints, but evidence for its use in the elbow remains limited. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the clinical, sports‐related and imaging outcomes of the minced cartilage technique in patients with unstable elbow osteochondritis dissecans (OCD).

pmc-13380917.title: A Case of Listeria monocytogenes Meningitis (Complicated) with Hydrocephalus and Occipital Lobe Infarction
pmc-13380917.creator: Meiyan Liu, Yuquan Chen, Pin Xie, Weijie Xu, Shuiwen Huang, Baorong Liu
pmc-13380917.description: BackgroundListeria monocytogenes (LM) meningitis is a rare but severe infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients, often leading to complications such as hydrocephalus, markedly increasing treatment complexity and the risk of poor outcomes.Case PresentationWe report a case of LM meningitis in an immunocompromised patient. The illness began with fever and gastrointestinal symptoms, followed by neck stiffness and altered consciousness.

pmc-13439369.title: Choline metabolism drives metastasis in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancers by activating FAM3C
pmc-13439369.creator: Cong Wang, Xuexia Xie, Jiahuang Li, Jiawei Zhu, Binghe Sun, Yue Wu, Wanying Zhang, Dake Li, Guo Chen

pmc-13443294.title: Association between BDNF and postoperative cognitive dysfunction across surgical stages: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13443294.creator: Danyan Liang, Xiaodong Wang, Yi Qiu
pmc-13443294.description: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a frequent complication after surgery, particularly among older adults, and its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a key regulator of neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, and has been implicated in POCD but published findings are inconsistent.
